summary: Lata Chhatre works in philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She taught Nguyen Van Hoa and held posts at Savitribai Phule Pune University as Reader in the Department of Philosophy (attested 2009) and Visiting Faculty (attested 2026).

Lata Deokar specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She served as a Research Assistant at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2001–2004) and as Visiting Faculty at Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 2026).

Lati Rinpoche (1922–2010) was a Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy scholar who studied at Ganden Shartse and Gyuto Monasteries. He was abbot of Ganden Shartse Monastery (~1976–1984) and a visiting scholar at the University of Virginia in 1976.
Latika Lahiri (b. 1923) is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Peking University and under Xianlin Ji (~1957–1961), and later held a post at the University of Delhi.

Laura Harrington works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She studied at Columbia University under Ryuichi Abe, Theodore Riccardi Jr., Gary A. Tubb, Lobsang Jamspal, Kirti Rinpoche, Tenzin Norbu, Nathaniel Dickson, and Gregory Hillis.

Lauran R. Hartley is a Tibetologist who held positions at Rutgers University, the Latse Contemporary Tibetan Cultural Library, and Indiana University Bloomington. She is Adjunct Assistant Professor and Director of the Modern Tibetan Studies Program at Columbia University (attested 2026).

Laurence Austine Waddell (1854–1938) studied medicine at the University of Glasgow. Working in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology, he served in the British and Indian military medical services, at Kolkata's Medical College, and as Professor of Tibetan at UCL (1906–1908).

Laurence Binyon (1869–1943) was a scholar of history, archaeology, Sinology, and Japanology who studied at Trinity College, Oxford. He worked at the British Museum (~1893–1933) and Harvard University (~1933–1934), and taught Arthur Waley.

Laurence Khantipalo Mills (1932–2021) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under teachers including Sangharakshita, Acharya Buddharakkhita, Chien Ming Chen, Dhardo Rinpoche, Namkhai Norbu, and Dudjom Rinpoche. He served as abbot at Wat Buddha Dhamma in 1978.

Laurie L. Patton (b. 1961), an Indology and religious studies scholar, earned her PhD at the University of Chicago. She held professorships at Emory and Duke, and served as president of Middlebury College (2015–2024) and the American Academy of Arts and Sciences (~2024).
Lavanya V. Eswar is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. She is attested in 2026 as a Ph.D. scholar at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, studying under doctoral supervisor V. Yamuna Devi.

Lawrence E. Sullivan (b. 1949) specializes in religious studies, history, and archaeology. He served as Director at Harvard University (attested 2000–2004) and Professor of Theology at the University of Notre Dame (attested 2005).

Lawrence Heyworth Mills (1837–1918) was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and Indology. He studied at New York University and served as a professor at the University of Oxford (attested 1903).

Lawrence J. McCrea is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and linguistics who studied under Sheldon Pollock. He serves as a Professor at Cornell University (attested 2026) and has taught James McHugh and Whitney Cox.

Lawrence William Nelson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed a doctorate at the California Institute of Integral Studies and also studied at Butler, Indiana, NYU, Northwestern, St. John's College, and other institutions.

Laxmanshastri Joshi (1901–1994) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied under Kevalananda Saraswati (~1923–1932) and served as Director of Prajna Pathashala from approximately 1935 to 1994.
Laxmidhar Behera is a scholar in computational studies and Indology. He has held academic posts at IIT Kanpur and IIT Mandi, and taught Jivnesh Sandhan.
LeRoy Carr Barret (1877–1960) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Washington and Lee University and at Johns Hopkins University (~1899–1903), where he studied under Maurice Bloomfield.

Leah Judith Zahler was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who completed her PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins (1980–1981). Her teachers also included Harvey B. Aronson and Geshe Wangyal.

Lee Yearley works in religious studies, philosophy, and Sinology. He held a professorship at Stanford University (attested 1989–1992), where he later became Professor Emeritus (attested 2026), and taught Thomas A. Tweed.
